extracted.intended_audience: photojournalists, journalism scholars, visual communication researchers, editors selecting press images
extracted.subtask_description: Framework and checklist for evaluating the newsworthiness of press photographs, identifying image-inherent, compositional, discursive and aesthetic factors that influence selection and meaning in news publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Denotative meaning of represented participants — who is shown, what is happening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of two broad factors shaping visual news values; the literal content and actors in the frame determine part of an image's newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Connotative meaning produced via camera and technical choices (shutter speed, lens, angle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The other broad shaping factor; photographic techniques inflect meaning, mood and emphasis and so affect news value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to elite persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of famous or elite individuals in the image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craig's photographic news value: famous faces increase an image's newsworthiness and likelihood of selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of compositional devices such as rule of thirds, framing and balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craig's value emphasizing formal composition; balance, framing and compositional rules draw attention and make an image 'picture-worthy'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on an individual human face or personal detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craig's value: images that personalize events (individual faces) increase audience connection and news appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negativity
rubrics_metrics.description: Depiction of suffering, damage, or other negative outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craig's value: negative events/affect (suffering, damage) are more newsworthy; editors favor images that show negative consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict / Dramatization
rubrics_metrics.description: Visible tension, conflict or dramatized action in the photo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craig's value: images that visualize conflict or dramatize events have higher news appeal because they show tension and stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damage
rubrics_metrics.description: Visible destruction in the image (e.g., destroyed property, wreckage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in newer image-inherent research as a selection criterion: visible destruction increases perceived newsworthiness and publishability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violence / Aggression
rubrics_metrics.description: Depiction of violent or aggressive actions, often captured as action shots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action/violence is an image-inherent factor that editors commonly prioritize for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controversy
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjects or scenes that are provocative or likely to generate dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provocative or controversial images are more likely to be selected because they attract attention and discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Celebrities
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of famous faces or public figures in the image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recurring image-inherent factor (overlaps with 'reference to elite persons') — celebrity presence increases publishability, especially for tabloids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unexpectedness
rubrics_metrics.description: Surprising or uncommon tableaux or moments captured by the photographer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unexpectedness makes images stand out and be considered 'worth publishing' because they offer novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotions
rubrics_metrics.description: Visible affect — expressions of feeling displayed by subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emotional display increases audience engagement; emotional clarity in an image is a strong selection criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution and technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographic craft — technical quality, exposure, focus, timing, and composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors consider photographic execution; technically well-made images are more likely to be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexuality / Eroticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Sexual imagery or erotic content, which is more prominent in tabloid contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sexual content functions as an image-inherent news value in certain markets (especially tabloids) and can drive selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetic News Value
rubrics_metrics.description: Press photographs can construe news events as aesthetically appealing — beauty becomes a news value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caple's addition: balance, color and composition draw attention; 'picture-worthy' moments and beauty themselves can be reasons for publishing images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discursive Construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual news values are constructed through multiple discursive elements rather than inherent solely in images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caple emphasizes that content, camera technique, caption and layout together construct an image's newsworthiness—selection and meaning are negotiated across these elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content (what is included)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specific people, objects and events shown in the image — what is included or excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of discursive construction: content choices determine denotative meaning and which news narratives an image can support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camera technique (how captured)
rubrics_metrics.description: How technical choices (angle, lens, shutter speed, framing) shape connotation and emphasis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of discursive construction: technique influences interpretation (e.g., low angle for heroism) and thus news value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption (verbal anchoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: Text accompanying the image that anchors or frames its meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captions provide verbal context that can fix interpretations, highlight certain actors or causes, and increase an image's suitability for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layout (placement on page)
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical placement and prominence of the image within publication layout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placement (size, position) constructs importance and guides audience attention; layout decisions interact with image selection and perceived newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisive moment capture
rubrics_metrics.description: Capturing the decisive, defining instant of an event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit criterion: the 'decisive moment' makes an image newsworthy by freezing a telling or climactic instant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faces and emotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of faces and visible emotional expression in the frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicitly valued because faces personalize and humanize news stories, increasing audience empathy and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic action
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear depiction of action that dramatizes the event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit criterion: action that dramatizes an occurrence increases immediacy and editorial interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beauty and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Aesthetic harmony and compositional quality that make an image visually appealing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit criterion overlapping with 'Aesthetic News Value' and 'Composition': beauty itself can be a selection rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Perceived authenticity or documentary status of the image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit: images that convey documentary truth (credibility, factuality) are valued for their evidentiary function in news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iconic potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Capacity of an image to become symbolic or widely recognized beyond the immediate event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicitly valued: images with iconic potential are prioritized because they can encapsulate and represent broader meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict visualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability of the image to make conflict visible and comprehensible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit: visuals that clearly show conflict help narrativize events and are therefore more newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Famous person
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of a recognizable public figure in the frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit restatement of celebrity/elite person criteria: famous people increase attention and selection likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetic quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall visual quality judged in terms of beauty, composition, color, balance and craft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit and explicit across Caple's framework: high aesthetic quality can itself function as a news value, rendering an image 'picture-worthy'.
